What Happens When Gliese 710 Passes Through the Oort Cloud?
What Happens When a Star Passes Through Our Solar System? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-jImX5h7ws Sunlight reaches Earth in about eight minutes, yet it would take months to travel out to the distant Oort Cloud where the orange dwarf Gliese 710 is heading. When the star passes through in about 1.3 million years, its gravity will brush through that vast cloud of icy bodies and nudge the comets nearest its path. Sources: Bailer-Jones (2022), The Astrophysical Journal Letters 935 L9 — Gaia DR3

How Close Will Gliese 710 Come to the Sun?
What Happens When a Star Passes Through Our Solar System? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-jImX5h7ws Gaia measurements put Gliese 710's closest approach at about a fifth of a light-year — roughly 13,000 times the Earth–Sun distance. If the gap between the Sun and Earth were one centimetre, Neptune would sit 30 centimetres away on a ruler, and Gliese 710 would pass more than 100 metres away, the length of a football pitch. Sources: Bailer-Jones (2022), The Astrophysical Journal Letters 935 L9

If Voyager Needs 75,000 Years, How Far Is the Nearest Star?
How Far Is the Nearest Star? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c5AdqQsnnys Voyager 1 leaves the solar system at about seventeen kilometres every second. At that speed, reaching the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, would take about 75,000 years. Sources: NASA JPL Voyager Mission Status (Voyager 1 heliocentric speed ~17 km/s) · Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023 (A&A 674, A1), Proxima Centauri at 4.24 light-years. How Thin Are Saturn's Rings?
How Long Do Saturn's Rings Have Left? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=55AEQwvs36g Saturn's main rings span tens of thousands of kilometres across, yet in places they are only about ten metres thick — ten times thinner than a 100-metre playing field. Drop through those ten metres and you are in open space again.
